# Orphan Worlds: Component Stats & Ship Assembly

**In short:** the numbers a component design carries (eleven common fields plus a small type block), reference values for every tier 1–2 type, the formulas that assemble components into a ship's figures, and how an organisation's understanding (0 to 10) turns rated figures into as-built ones, with variance per hull. Section 7 sizes three rival bids for one bulk hauler (HR-1) to show the model at work.

*Status:* draft. Everything here is **Candidate**. Tables and figures in sections 4, 6 and 7 are generated by `scripts/components/build_doc.py` from the data files beside it (`components.json`, `rules.json`, `hr1.json`); change the data, not the tables. Drive figures agree with *Drives & Transit* section 3. Corvane orbits in section 7 use its layout (Iver 0.50 AU, Halden IV 0.80 AU).

> **Repo note:** `scripts/components/` isn't in this repo yet; the tables below are as last generated.

*Companion documents:* *Design Document*, *Salvage & Research*, *Component Catalogue* (this answers its open questions on which numbers a component carries, how they combine, and how as-built versions are handled), *Drives & Transit* (orbits, drive families, transit times) and *Requirements & Bids* (uses the stat names, understanding modifiers and HR-1 distributions defined here).

---

## 1. Principles **(Candidate)**

- **Few numbers.** Eleven common fields and two to five type fields per design. Everything else (cost, jet power, radiator rejection, boil-off, ship figures) is derived.
- **Each number matters to a decision.** If no bid, salvage or reverse-engineering choice turns on a figure, it goes.
- **Physical where possible.** Tonnes, MW, km/s, days. Ship figures come from the rocket equation, ½ F v_e and T⁴, so results never contradict physics, and a player who knows no physics can still read them.
- **Legible.** Every ship figure traces back to named components and one understanding number per organisation and type. Reports say "heavier because Arden's NTR understanding is Basic", not "−7%".
- **Rated and as-built.** Designs carry rated figures. What gets built is rated × understanding modifiers × instance variance. Uncertainty comes from people and organisations, which the player can see and influence.
- **Data first.** Every record maps to a flat data file with the same field names as this document.

## 2. Common stat block **(Candidate)**

Every component design carries these fields (names from the shared brief, plus `reject_temp`). Values are rated, for one unit in its operating state (a drive while thrusting).

| Field | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mass` | t | Dry mass of one unit. Parametric designs (tanks, radiators, frames, cargo gear, shelters) take mass from their type block; their effort, inputs and spares are then per tonne. |
| `cost` | cr | Derived, never entered: inputs at reference prices plus `build_effort` × labour rate. Reference: metals 2 kcr/t, rare metals 500 kcr/t, components 200 kcr/unit, labour 5 kcr per effort-day. Local prices come from the economy. |
| `build_effort` | ed | Effort-days: one yard or works team for one day. Sets build time against capacity. |
| `inputs` | t, units | `metals`, `rare_metals`, `components`, optional `water`; consumed at build. Fissile fuel counts as rare metals for now. |
| `power` | MWe | Positive generates, negative draws, in operating state. Solar is rated at 1 S (Earth insolation) and scales with local flux. |
| `heat` | MWt | Waste heat sent to the ship's radiators in operating state. Always ≥ 0; radiator capacity lives in the radiator block. |
| `reject_temp` | K | Temperature at which `heat` leaves the component. A radiator only takes heat from sources at or above its own temperature. |
| `reliability` | d | Mean time between faults (MTBF) in days in service. |
| `maintenance` | units/yr, people | `spares` consumed per year in service; `crew` needed for upkeep. |
| `crew` | people | Operating crew attributable to the component, watches included. Fractions allowed; the ship total rounds up. |
| `signature` | MW | Infrared emitted directly rather than through radiators: plume or thruster body while thrusting, RTG fins, radar while active. |

Identity fields: `id`, `name`, `category`, `type`, `tier`, `origin`, `scaling` (unit, per_t_propellant, per_MWt, per_t_cargo, per_berth, fraction) and `block` (the type block's name). Documentation level belongs to each holder, not to the design.

**Reliability as MTBF.** Chosen over an annual failure chance because:
- rates add: ship faults per year = Σ 365 / MTBF, never capped at 1;
- any trip length converts: the chance of no fault over t days is exp(−t / MTBF);
- understanding scales it with one multiplier;
- it reads well ("about five years between faults"), with higher meaning better, as the field name implies.

A fault takes the unit out until the crew repair it with spares. Repair time and severity belong to the operations model.

**Departures from the brief (flagged):**
- `reject_temp` is added; it's needed to make T⁴ matter.
- `heat` is never negative.
- `signature` is direct emission in MW, so ship signature = radiated heat + Σ `signature`.
- `build_effort` uses one unit (effort-days) for both yards and works.
- The brief's thrust classes fit small ships. Loaded haulers are slower: NTR about 0.01 to 0.09 g, NEP about 0.02 to 0.04 mg.

## 3. Type-specific blocks **(Candidate)**

| Category | Block | Fields (unit) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Power | `solar` | `electric_output` (MWe at 1 S) | Inner system only. |
| | `reactor` | `thermal_output` (MWt), `electric_output` (MWe, 0 if bare), `fuel_life` (yr at full output) | RTGs have both outputs; fission reactors feed conversion. |
| | `conversion` | `efficiency`, `rated_input` (MWt) | Output = input × efficiency; heat = input − output at `reject_temp`. |
| Thermal | `radiator` | `reject_temp` (K), `areal_mass` (kg/m²), `emissivity` | Derived `specific_rejection` (MWt/t) = 2εσT⁴ / areal_mass; sized in MWt per ship. |
| Drives | `drive` | `exhaust_velocity` (km/s), `thrust` (kN), `propellant`, `efficiency` (jet power / input), `thrust_class` (low, moderate, high), `auxiliary` | Jet power = ½ × thrust × v_e (kN × km/s = MW). Thermal: core MWt = jet / efficiency. Electric: draw = jet / efficiency. |
| Propellant | `tank` | `propellant`, `tank_fraction` (t per t propellant), `boil_off` (%/day passive), `cooling_power` (MWe per kt, zero boil-off) | Hydrogen needs cryogenic storage. |
| Structure | `frame` | `mass_fraction` by thrust class | Frame = fraction × carried mass. |
| | `hull`, `armour`, `shielding` | `volume` (m³); `area` (m²), `protection` (MJ per hit); `mass_per_berth`, `dose_factor` | Habitat modules include their own hull. Shelters are mostly water (double duty). |
| Habitation | `habitat` | `berths`, `volume` (m³), `gravity` (g, spin only) | |
| | `life_support`, `medical` | `capacity` (people), `closure` (0 to 1), `consumables` (t per person-year); `capacity` | |
| Sensors & comms | `sensor`, `comms` | `detect_range` (AU for a 1 MW source, scales with √signature) or `range_km`; `range` (AU) | Detection rules belong to combat. |
| Command & computing | `navigation`, `fire_control` | `correction_overhead` (fraction of Δv); `track_quality` (0 to 1) | Automation (tier 3): `crew_factor`. |
| Weapons | `weapon`, `missile` | launcher `muzzle_velocity`, `projectile_mass`, `rate`, `magazine`; point defence `range_km`, `intercept`; countermeasures `decoys`; missile `delta_v`, `accel_g`, `warhead` | Light by design. |
| Utility | `cargo`, `lander`, `work_rate` | `mass_per_t_cargo`, `handling_rate` (t/day); `payload`, `delta_v`; `rate` (t/day) | |

**Performance group.** Understanding scales one group of fields per block:
- drive: `exhaust_velocity` and `thrust`
- reactor: `thermal_output`
- conversion: `efficiency`
- radiator: capacity
- solar: `electric_output`
- tank: `boil_off` and `cooling_power` (divided)
- life support: `consumables` (divided)
- sensors and weapons: their range or main figure

**Physics checks.**
- **Jet power.** Kestrel: ½ × 250 kN × 9 km/s = 1,125 MW. At efficiency 0.94 the core runs at 1,197 MWt, almost all of which leaves with the hydrogen, so its radiator load is only decay and gamma heating (0.5 MWt). Thrust-to-weight 2.5.
- **Electric drive.** A Sable Hall cluster turns 2.0 MWe into 1.20 MW of jet (efficiency 0.6). Of the 0.8 MW lost, 0.12 MWt goes to the radiators and 0.68 MW radiates from the thruster body (its `signature`).
- **Reactor to electric.** Sable reactor 30 MWt through three turbines at 0.25 gives 7.5 MWe and 22.5 MWt to reject at 650 K.
- **Radiators.** Specific rejection = 2εσT⁴ / areal mass, with no sink. Plate at 350 K: 0.121 MWt/t (83 t per 10 MWt). Fanfold at 650 K: 1.72 MWt/t (5.8 t per 10 MWt). Hot conversion heat is cheap to reject; habitat, electronics and cryocooler heat at 350 K is expensive.
- **Hydrogen.** LH2 is 70.8 kg/m³, so one sphere per kt has 2,826 m² of surface. At 0.35 W/m² through insulation the leak is 0.99 kW per kt, boiling off 0.019 %/day. A 20 K cryocooler at 20% of Carnot stops it for 0.082 MWe per kt. Tankage is 0.12 t/t, against 0.03 t/t for water.

## 5. Ship assembly **(Candidate)**

A ship design is a list of parts (`design`, `count`, `min_working`, options such as `active_cooling`), a cargo capacity, a `target_dv` and a `radiator_margin`. At design time the model solves and stores the sizes: propellant to meet `target_dv`, radiator capacity to close the heat balance × (1 + margin), and frame mass by thrust class. As-built hulls keep those sizes; only the components change.

Formulas (thrust in kN and mass in t, so F / m is in m/s²):

| Figure | Rule |
|---|---|
| Dry mass | Σ unit masses + tanks (`tank_fraction` × propellant) + radiators (capacity / specific rejection) + cargo gear (0.05 × cargo) + shelter (2 t × berths) + frame (`mass_fraction` × (other dry mass + cargo)) |
| Wet mass | dry + cargo + propellant |
| Ship v_e | ΣF / Σ(F_i / v_e,i) over main drives (auxiliary thrusters excluded) |
| Δv | loaded: v_e ln(wet / (dry + cargo)); empty: v_e ln((dry + propellant) / dry) |
| Acceleration | full: ΣF / wet; empty: ΣF / (dry + cargo); shown in mg below 0.01 g, otherwise g |
| Power balance | generation (solar × flux, conversion output, RTGs) ≥ housekeeping (all other draws, cryocoolers) + electric drives; if short, electric drives throttle to (generation − housekeeping) / demand |
| Heat balance | sources go hottest first to radiators at or below their `reject_temp`; if heat is left over, reactors derate until it closes |
| Crew | max(2, ⌈Σ(`crew` + `maintenance.crew`)⌉); berths and life-support capacity must cover it; consumables = crew × `consumables` |
| Faults per year | Σ 365 / MTBF over every instance |
| Clean-trip chance | product over critical groups of P(at least `min_working` of n units survive t days), each unit exp(−t / MTBF); critical = drives, power, thermal, propellant, life support, navigation |
| Cost | Σ inputs × price + (E_comp + E_int) × labour rate, with E_int = 0.15 × E_comp |
| Build time | lead + max(E_comp / teams, largest single unit / 8 teams) + E_int / min(teams, 20); lead = 30 d × tier × documentation factor (section 6) for the slowest design the organisation has not built before |
| Upkeep | spares × 200 kcr + crew × 150 kcr per year; spares = Σ `maintenance.spares` × failure multiplier |
| Signature | coasting: radiated heat + Σ non-drive `signature`; burning: plus drive `signature` |

**Validation.**
- **Invalid:**
  - a design below the organisation's minimum understanding for its documentation level
  - drive propellant with no matching tank (hydrogen needs cryogenic storage)
  - housekeeping power not met
  - heat that can't close even with reactors fully derated
  - berths or life support below crew
  - a relic type the organisation doesn't physically hold
- **Derated** (valid, weaker): electric drives throttled or reactors below rating. Shown on the bid and the ship.
- **Fails the requirement** (a bid matter): cargo, Δv, crew, budget or deadline missed.
- **Warnings:** trips over 120 days without medical; passive hydrogen storage on long transits; a critical group with no redundancy.

## 6. Rated, as-built and understanding **(Candidate)**

**Three layers.**
- *Design* (rated): the documented figures, the same for every holder.
- *As-built version:* one per organisation and design, created when the organisation operationalises it. It holds the mean multipliers at the organisation's effective understanding at that time. When understanding later rises by a full point, re-operationalising creates v2.
- *Instance:* each built unit draws its own multipliers around the version's means and keeps them for life, so two hulls from one yard differ.

**Understanding scale.** 0 to 10 per organisation and component type, stored as a decimal and shown as a band: 0 None, 1–2 Rudimentary, 3–4 Basic, 5–6 Competent, 7–8 Advanced, 9–10 Mastery. Whether the player sees the exact value for organisations the state doesn't own is for the bids document.

**Documentation.** Effective understanding u_eff = u + offset, clamped to 0–10.

| Documentation | Offset | Minimum u to build | Cap on gains from production | Tooling lead factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Complete | +1 | 1 | 10 | 1.0 |
| Working | 0 | 2 | 9 | 1.3 |
| Partial | −1 | 4 | 8 | 1.7 |
| Fragmentary | −2 | 6 | 6 | 2.5 |

**Modifier curves.** With deficit d = (10 − u_eff) / 10, one shape and four coefficients:
- **Means:**
  - mass × (1 + 0.40 d²)
  - performance × (1 − 0.15 d²)
  - failure rate × (1 + 3.0 d²), so MTBF is divided by the same
  - build effort × (1 + 1.0 d²)
- **Variance per instance**, linear in d and never zero, with draws clipped at ±2.5 σ:
  - mass σ = 1% + 8% d
  - performance σ = 0.5% + 3% d
  - failure rate lognormal σ = 0.05 + 0.40 d
  - effort σ = 2% + 15% d
- Inputs scale with as-built mass, cost follows inputs and effort, and spares follow the failure multiplier.

| Understanding (band) | Mass x | Performance x | MTBF x | Effort x | SD mass | SD perf | SD fail (log) | SD effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (None) | 1.400 | 0.850 | 0.25 | 2.00 | 9.0% | 3.5% | 0.45 | 17.0% |
| 2 (Rudimentary) | 1.256 | 0.904 | 0.34 | 1.64 | 7.4% | 2.9% | 0.37 | 14.0% |
| 4 (Basic) | 1.144 | 0.946 | 0.48 | 1.36 | 5.8% | 2.3% | 0.29 | 11.0% |
| 6 (Competent) | 1.064 | 0.976 | 0.68 | 1.16 | 4.2% | 1.7% | 0.21 | 8.0% |
| 8 (Advanced) | 1.016 | 0.994 | 0.89 | 1.04 | 2.6% | 1.1% | 0.13 | 5.0% |
| 10 (Mastery) | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.0% | 0.5% | 0.05 | 2.0% |

Quadratic means give large early gains (Basic 4 to Competent 6 more than halves the mass penalty) and little at the top. Linear variance keeps even good yards slightly unpredictable.

**Learning.**
- *Production:* completing the n-th unit of a type adds 0.6 / n to u, up to the cap of the best documentation held for that type. Cumulative gain after n units: 1 unit +0.60, 2 units +0.90, 4 units +1.25, 8 units +1.63, 16 units +2.03, 32 units +2.44. That is about +0.4 per doubling (0.6 × ln 2): Wright's law in understanding terms.
- *Use:* each instance-year in service adds 0.05 to the operator's u for that type (same cap). This is how a shipping firm learns about the ships it runs.
- Study of finds, staff moves, spillover and decay are research and character matters (*Salvage & Research*) acting on the same scale.

## 7. Worked example: HR-1 bulk hauler **(Candidate)**

**Requirement HR-1** (state, Corvane): 400 t of cargo Iver → Halden IV; Δv ≥ 10 km/s loaded (provisional); crew ≤ 12; budget 60.0 Mcr; deadline 400 days of build time (yard start to rollout; design and trials come on top).

**Assumptions:**
- Orbits are the working values from *Drives & Transit*: a star of 0.75 solar masses (luminosity 0.30), Iver at 0.50 AU, Halden IV at 0.80 AU. They're treated as circular and coplanar, ignoring planetary departure and capture.
- Solar arrays are sized for the 0.47 S at Halden IV.
- A Hohmann transfer needs 7.54 km/s and takes 111 days. Impulsive ships here spend 90% of loaded Δv on the fastest tangent-departure transfer (98 d at 8 km/s, 83 d at 10, 73 d at 12). NEP ships spiral at the Edelbaum Δv of 7.64 km/s.
- Support designs are common pre-collapse records. Tier 1 types default to understanding 5 and tier 2 to 4, unless listed.

| Understanding (u, documentation → u_eff) | Iver | Arden | Morrow |
|---|---|---|---|
| NTR solid-core | 6 complete → 7 | 4 working → 4 | 4 working → 4 |
| NEP ion/Hall | 2 working → 2 | 4 working → 4 | 5 partial → 4 |
| Fission, compact | 4 working → 4 | 4 working → 4 | 4 partial → 3 |
| Power conversion (turbine) | 4 working → 4 | 4 working → 4 | 4 partial → 3 |
| Cryogenic storage | 5 complete → 6 | 4 working → 4 | 4 working → 4 |
| Deployable radiators | 4 complete → 5 | 4 working → 4 | 4 working → 4 |
| Frames (structure) | 7 working → 7 | 5 working → 5 | 5 working → 5 |
| Yard: teams, labour kcr/ed | 60, 5 | 24, 5 | 25, 6.5 |
| Tooling lead d | 60 | 78 | 102 |

- **Iver Yard Company** (Bold, Ambitious) builds three Kestrels from its complete record, with active cryocooling, deployable radiators and a large margin (target 11.5 km/s). It's the biggest ship, carrying 2,198 t of LH2 (31,046 m³).
- **Arden Orbital Works** (Cautious, Traditionalist) uses two smaller Terns from a working-level record, fixed radiators with a 25% margin, passive LH2 storage (losing 32 t per trip), one bunkhouse sized exactly to the crew, and no sickbay. Much cheaper than Iver on paper, with a cautious target of 11.0 km/s.
- **Morrow Ice & Freight** (Innovative, Opportunistic) rebuilds its salvaged Sable NEP hauler from partial records: one reactor, three turbines, three Hall clusters, water propellant, radiators with no margin, a leased berth. A target of 12.0 km/s is cheap at v_e 30. Transit time isn't in the requirement, so Morrow doesn't design for it: a second reactor would nearly halve the trip, but push crew past 12 and cost well past the budget.

| As-built, P10 to P90 | Iver | Arden | Morrow |

| Build time d | 233 to 253 | 377 to 433 | 353 to 379 |

**What the player should read from it.**
- **Iver** delivers close to its claims (NTR u_eff 7): Δv 11.17 against 11.50 rated, and cost 63.6 Mcr against a 60.0 Mcr budget (over budget in 59% of builds). The real cost is hydrogen: about 18.6 kt of water electrolysed per one-way trip, some 6 months of Halden's ice quarry at the 3.2 kt per month in the presentation sketches. Extra Δv buys time slowly (98, 83 and 73 d with 8, 10 and 12 km/s spent), but Iver's margin also buys freedom from waiting for transfer windows.
- **Arden** looks safe on paper, but its NTR understanding is Basic. As-built v_e falls about 5.4% and mass rises about 14%, so Δv drops from 11.00 to 9.78 km/s. 41% of hulls miss 10 km/s, and 61% miss the deadline on its small yard. Trials would reveal this: the risk register's "surprise in trials", explained by a visible number.
- **Morrow** is light and frugal (865 t wet, 212 t of water per trip) but slow (281 d rated, 328 d as-built) and fragile. Its reactor and turbines come from partial records (u_eff 3), so as-built heat no longer closes with zero radiator margin: the reactor runs at 90%, the drives at 93%, and the chance of a clean trip falls from 65% to 35%. The single reactor is a single point of failure. The bid meets the letter of HR-1, but a loaded leg takes most of a year.
- **Cost scale.** A 400 t hauler costs 38.6 to 63.6 Mcr and takes 216 to 404 days to build. Labour is 70% to 81% of cost and components 14% to 22%. But components are the scarce resource: 32 to 61 units per hull plus 10 to 20 units a year in spares, against the 18 units a month Port Arden is already short in the presentation sketches.

## 8. Data-file shape **(Candidate)**

The prototype sketch in `scripts/components/` has three files: `components.json` (designs), `rules.json` (prices, understanding coefficients, documentation table, assembly constants, placeholder orbits) and `hr1.json` (requirement, organisations, ship designs). Records as the script emits them:

```jsonc
// component design (rated); cost is derived, never entered
{"id": "kestrel_ntr", "name": "Kestrel NTR", "category": "drives", "type": "ntr_solid_core", "tier": 2, "origin": "pre_collapse", "scaling": "unit", "mass": 10.0, "build_effort": 500, "inputs": {"metals": 7.0, "rare_metals": 1.5, "components": 5.0}, "power": -0.05, "heat": 0.5, "reject_temp": 650, "reliability": 2000, "maintenance": {"spares": 1.5, "crew": 0.5}, "crew": 0.0, "signature": 300, "block": "drive", "drive": {"exhaust_velocity": 9.0, "thrust": 250, "propellant": "hydrogen", "efficiency": 0.94, "thrust_class": "moderate"}}
// as-built version: one per organisation and design, mean multipliers at operationalisation
{"id": "iver_yard/kestrel_ntr/v1", "design": "kestrel_ntr", "org": "iver_yard", "documentation": "complete", "u_eff": 7, "mass_mult": 1.036, "perf_mult": 0.987, "fail_mult": 1.27, "effort_mult": 1.09, "units_built": 0}
// as-built instance: drawn once at build, then carries its own history
{"id": "IYC-HR1-1/kestrel_ntr/1", "version": "iver_yard/kestrel_ntr/v1", "mass": 9.95, "exhaust_velocity": 8.88, "thrust": 246.7, "reliability": 1717, "build_effort": 589, "service_days": 0, "faults": 0}
// ship design (bid); sizes are solved at design time and stored with it
{"id": "IYC-HR1", "org": "iver_yard", "cargo": 400, "target_dv": 11.5, "radiator_margin": 0.1, "parts": [{"design": "kestrel_ntr", "count": 3, "min_working": 2}, {"design": "rime_lh2", "active_cooling": true}, {"design": "brightleaf_array", "count": 3, "min_working": 2}, "..."]}
```

- Field names match sections 2 and 3; one type block per design, keyed by `block`.
- Organisation records hold `understanding_type` (by type), `understanding_category` (fallback), `understanding_default` (by tier), `documentation` (by design id), `operationalised` (design ids already built) and `yard` (`teams`, `labour_rate`).
- `cost` and other derived figures are computed on load and never stored, so data cannot drift.

## 9. Open questions

- **Drives and transit:**
  - final v_e, thrust and mass per family
  - NEP propellant (water here, provisionally); NTR on water
  - real Corvane orbits; planetary departure and capture Δv
  - whether 10 km/s suits HR-1: a Hohmann hop needs 7.54 km/s, so it allows one loaded leg with a modest margin, and returns need refuelling at Halden
  - how to show Δv buying freedom from windows rather than speed
- **Reconciled with *Drives & Transit*:** its family values (LH2 tankage 0.15 t/t, water 0.04 t/t, 0.05 %/day boil-off, NEP v_e 35) were conservative typical values. Ships use this document's design values (0.12, 0.03, 0.019 %/day; the Sable Hall cluster at v_e 30, inside its optimum range). Its revised drive table (water NTR 3.2 km/s, NEP 0.05 mg) agrees with the designs here.
- **Carbon:** the Corbel and Pinion engines burn methalox, but carbon is not in the resource list. Either add carbon or switch tier 1 chemical designs to hydrolox from water (v_e 4.4), as *Drives & Transit* suggests.
- **Hydrogen supply:** electrolysis and liquefaction as infrastructure (power, ice throughput). It may make NTR haulers impractical early, which could be the right outcome.
- **Fissile fuel:** its own resource or part of rare metals; refuelling (`fuel_life`) and NTR core wear (burn hours) as maintenance.
- **Faults:** repair time, degraded vs disabled, loss of ship; whether the player sees clean-trip chance or only faults per year.
- **Bids:** whether bidders quote rated or expected as-built figures, how traits bias quotes, and how much of u the player sees.
- **Operating states:** power and heat are checked in one state. Warships with radars or lasers may need coast and combat states, and possibly a third radiator temperature.
- **Components as a resource:** whether 1 unit ≈ 1 t of manufactured goods, and whether components rather than labour should dominate cost.
- **Learning:** rates untested; decay without practice and spillover between related types need numbers.
- **Yards:** team counts, reactivation of dormant yards, leasing terms (bids and economy).
- **Crew health:** spin gravity, medical and long-trip rules.
